newsitem.title: UK: BG demands regulator clarity over pricing.
newsitem.headline: BG demands regulator clarity over pricing.

text.p: BG Plc - formerly known as British Gas - told a thin gathering of shareholders on Wednesday it badly needed clarity in the near term on pricing policy to end a prolonged period of uncertainty regarding the group's prospects.
The MMC report on controversial price proposals from watchdog Ofgas is due by May 31 at the latest, but it is up to Ofgas to decide when the inquiry is actually published.

The MMC started its inquiry in October after BG rejected the Ofgas proposals, saying the proposed cuts in charges to gas suppliers would leave its pipeline operator TransCo with insufficient income to run a safe and reliable network.
BG argued Ofgas proposals would cost it 400 million stg in annual cash flow, while investors fear a big dividend cut if the regulator's plans become reality.
"During the last six months we have submitted more than 500 documents to the MMC, and strongly argued the merits of our case," chief executive David Varney said.

"It is essential for this MMC inquiry to provide TransCo with long term regulatory clarity and stability, which is vital for the successful implementation of full domestic competition by the end of 1998," Varney told shareholders.
The official deadline for nationwide competition is April 1998, but the opposition Labour party told Reuters yesterday it won't be tied to this timetable it wins the election on Thursday.
Besides the Ofgas price proposals, BG faces uncertainty over Labour's intention to introduce a windfall tax on utilities if it seizes power from the Conservatives.
The company said it had no idea how big this tax might be and added it had therefore refrained from making any in-house prognoses.
"We haven't got a clue what the tax will be," Varney told reporters after the shareholders meeting.
